title: Department of Land Resources successfully concludes Special Campaign 6 for institutionalising Swachhata and reducing pendency
subtitle: Significant achievements in cleanliness, grievance redressal and records management under Special Campaign 6
body_text: The Department of Land Resources, Ministry of Rural Development, successfully concluded its participation in Special Campaign 6, conducted from 2 nd to 31 st October 2026, under the guidance of the Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG). The campaign focused on institutionalising Swachhata, reducing pendency in Government offices, improving records management and promoting efficient utilisation of office space and resources. Demonstrating its commitment to efficient and citizen-centric governance, the Department achieved its target of conducting 100% cleanliness campaigns in and around its premises. Significant progress was also made in grievance redressal, with 100% disposal of public grievances and appeals during the campaign.  Further, 21 references received from Members of Parliament were disposed of. A focused exercise was undertaken for records management and digitisation.  A total number of 1449 physical files and 501 e-files were reviewed for recording, weeding out and closure, as applicable, contributing to better record management and streamlining of administrative processes.  The campaign also contributed to the effective utilisation of office space and disposal of redundant materials. In addition to cleanliness and administrative reforms, the Department placed emphasis on the health, well-being and capacity building of its employees.  Yoga sessions were organised at the Rejuve Wellness Centre located at the Department’s Shivaji Stadium Annexe office premises.  Debate and painting competitions on themes related to Swachhata were also conducted to encourage creativity, awareness and active participation among employees.  A session on Mental Health was organised in the Department as part of the campaign. The successful implementation of Special Campaign 6 reflects the Department of Land Resources’ continued commitment to promoting cleanliness, improving administrative efficiency, strengthening accountability and creating a  productive work environment. **** SS/HR
